\begin{theorem}[Influence and first-level Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.two_sub_totalInfluence_le_fourierWeightAtLevel_one_of_isBalanced}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p063-b008}
\label{FABL.two_sub_totalInfluence_le_fourierWeightAtLevel_one_of_isBalanced}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.isBalanced_iff_fourierCoeff_empty_eq_zero, FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_eq_one, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_card_mul_sq_fourierCoeff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ have mean zero under the uniform distribution on the cube.
For each coordinate, define its influence as the uniform average of the square of the
discrete derivative of $f$, and let the total influence be the sum of these coordinate
influences. For each subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let its Fourier weight be the
square of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$, and let the level-one Fourier weight be
the sum of these weights over all singleton subsets. Then $2-\mathrm{total\
influence}(f)\le \mathrm{level\text{-}one\ Fourier\ weight}(f)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive dimension of a balanced sign function]
\lean{FABL.positive_dimension_of_isBalanced}
\label{FABL.positive_dimension_of_isBalanced}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.mean, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a sign-valued function, viewed as real-valued. If its
uniform mean is zero, then $n>0$.
\end{theorem}
